I usually don't sit long with the dye except after I just bleached, I usually have the color in for 2 hours then.

In between the bleaches I only do quick re-dyes in the shower.

This is how it looked before the re-dye

I washed my hair with a normal shampoo (that has sulfate in it) to get rid of any build up and open the hair cuticles to get the dye to stick.

Then I brushed trough my wet hair with the tangle teezer brush and towel dried it slightly.

Mixing about 1/3 directions violet to 2/3 revlon nutri color 200 violet

I usually just use the brush for mixing. I then put the color on with my hands, with gloves on. Finally I run through it all with a comb to make sure the color gets as even as possible.

Then I just hop back in the shower and let the dye sit for about 15-20 minutes, rinse it out, put some conditioner on for a minute or 2 rinse that out, then blow dry it.

So this is how it looks right after blow drying. I have curly hair and when I want the curls to look good I don't blow dry.

Here is the final result after some straightening I'm standing under a very bright light and the color is more even looking in regular daylight.

The ends of the hair is always hardest to keep the color in. They are damaged from the bleaching and wear and tear so the dye takes a very long time to stick properly to them. I don't mind that much but if you do you need to keep the dye in for atleast an hour. You can just put a plastic bag over your hair and go about your business outside the shower until its time to rinse.
How I do quick re-dyeing in between bleaches
